title: 📖 The Moment That Defines It
paragraphs: 📖 The Moment That Defines It
When Nathan confronted David, it wasn’t to humiliate him.
It was to restore him.

Nathan didn’t post about David.
He didn’t gather a crowd.
He didn’t brand him forever as “the adulterer king.”

He told a story.
He pierced the conscience.
And when conviction came…
David repented.
“You are the man.” — 2 Samuel 12:7

Correction produced repentance.
Judgment would have produced rebellion.
⚖️ CALLING OUT vs BUILDING UP

The question isn’t:
“Should Christians ever confront?”
The real question is:
What spirit are we carrying when we do it?
Are we defending God… or defending ego?
Are we grieved… or secretly satisfied?
Do we want restoration… or reputation damage?

Public sin sometimes requires public clarity.
But even then — the goal must be redemption, not humiliation.
Correction becomes judgment when:
Mercy disappears
Restoration isn’t the goal
We speak about someone more than we pray for them
We enjoy exposing more than healing
Should Christians call out other Christians publicly?

When?
How?
Under what heart posture?
Let’s talk — but with humility.
Type “RESTORE” if you believe correction should lead to healing.
